verses.1: The wine that is worthless cannot be considered a reward, nor can anything that comes from it be regarded as valuable.
verses.2: They were like those who were punished by the king’s curse; their souls were filled with evil.
verses.3: Honor to the man who has put aside his disputes and all his enemies.
verses.4: From the ground that cannot be plowed, it cannot be cultivated. And he asked about the harvest and the olives.
verses.5: Deep waters are like thorns in one’s heart; and a person who is in distress will be destroyed.
verses.6: Many people will call out to those who show kindness and honesty. But who can truly be found among them?
verses.7: A righteous man walks in peace, and his children follow him.
verses.8: The king who sits on the throne of judgment is evil in his eyes. All that’s good about him is nothing.
verses.9: Who can say, “I have been forgiven; I am cleansed from my sins”?
verses.10: One stone and another stone, where and where will the wrath of Jehovah be poured out?
verses.11: Even in his faults, a young man can be recognized as good and virtuous if he acts rightly.
verses.12: He who hears and sees, God created both of them.
verses.13: Do not love evil, lest you lose your sight and be blind.
verses.14: “Bad, bad,” will say the singer. And then he will sing.
verses.15: There is gold, and many pearls, as well as all kinds of precious treasures of wisdom.
verses.16: Take it away, for it is a foreign city, and its people are barbarians.
verses.17: The man ate false bread, and after his stomach filled up, it became painful.
verses.18: Thoughts are made with wisdom and plans are formed for war.
verses.19: Golé-Sód walks around, with his mouth open; his lips never shut.
verses.20: He scorns his father and mother; they know that he is in darkness.
verses.21: The land is cursed from both the east and the west; it will not be blessed.
verses.22: Do not say, “Ashlamah-Ra’ kavu l’Yehova veyosh’la’k.”
verses.23: The LORD’s anger is like a mountain and a hill; it’s like the ears of a liar who doesn’t speak the truth.
verses.24: From God come the great deeds; who can understand His ways?
verses.25: Man’s efforts will only make things more sacred, and after that, there will be no more sanctity at all.
verses.26: The wicked are like a king who is wise; he sits upon them.
verses.27: The lamp of Jehovah is the spirit of man; it searches every hidden place.
verses.28: Mercy and truth will create a king, and they will support him with their grace.
verses.29: Glorification of those who possess strength and wisdom; and honor for the elderly.
verses.30: Wounds from tamaruk, and those from biting by rats.
